name: EPFL round-robin-arbiter, LUT-6 count
description: Optimise the EPFL combinational benchmark circuit round-robin-arbiter (a round-robin arbiter; 256 inputs, 129 outputs) with the logic-synthesis tool ABC and map it to lookup tables (LUTs) with at most 6 inputs, minimising the number of LUTs. The result must compute the same function as the original circuit.

sources.locator: Improvements to Technology Mapping for LUT-Based FPGAs
Circuit Minimization with QBF-Based Exact Synthesis
EPFL benchmark repository: arbiter circuit files and best_results/README.md (best LUT-6 counts and levels, 2026).

Amaru, Gaillardon and De Micheli (2015), The EPFL Combinational Benchmark Suite (title read in the PDF text): circuit descriptions and input/output counts for arbiter; a benchmark paper, so not primary evidence.

execution.interface: script() -> string of ABC commands separated by `;` or newlines. The evaluator runs `read <circuit>; <script>` in ABC and writes out the network the script leaves. That network must consist only of LUTs with at most 6 inputs (in ABC a LUT mapper such as `if -K 6` produces one; library gates or a wider node are invalid), and it must be equivalent to the original circuit, which a separate ABC process checks with `cec`. The script may not contain the characters ! / \ ~, may not use commands that read or write files, change the session or start other programs (read*, write*, load*, dump*, save* and their short forms, source, alias, set, unset, history, cd, ls, pwd, quit, exit), and may not ask for LUTs wider than 6 inputs (-K above 6). Time limits: 1200 s for the script, 900 s for the equivalence check. A script that is refused, fails, runs out of time or changes the function is invalid. Score: the number of LUTs with two or more inputs (buffers, inverters and constants are not counted), minimized.

limitations: Most records come from SAT-based exact synthesis of subcircuits, which an ABC script cannot express.
Requires the Berkeley ABC binary (set ARNEW_ABC).
LUTs and levels are counted from the written network by the convention of the EPFL table (single-input nodes are free), not from ABC's print_stats.
The record was reproduced by this task's verifier from a published solution (or an optimiser run). See VALIDITY.md.

checks: the published circuit has 259 LUTs and 93 levels (EPFL convention), largest LUT 6 inputs
ABC cec (inputs and outputs matched by name): equivalent to the benchmark circuit

The evidence must explain why the problem matters and how the local task represents it. Using a task to evaluate an agent, framework, or general-purpose model, or citing only a benchmark, dataset, or tool, does not establish scientific importance.
science_relevance.reason: The cited papers have LUT technology mapping and the minimisation of benchmark circuits as their main objective, and the evaluator scores exactly the LUT count or level count of an equivalence-checked 6-LUT network; the local candidate is an ABC script, which is narrower than the methods of the record holders.
science_relevance.scientific_problem: Implement the EPFL benchmark circuit arbiter as a network of lookup tables with at most six inputs, with an ABC command script, minimising the size (LUT count for size, LUT levels for depth).
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Mapping logic to k-input lookup tables fixes the area and delay of an FPGA implementation, and the EPFL suite is the community reference for logic optimisation, with best LUT-6 counts and levels lowered by new synthesis methods every few years. A better result is a smaller or shallower implementation of a standard circuit; the best-known networks mostly come from SAT-based exact synthesis, which a script of ABC commands cannot express.

papers.title: Improvements to Technology Mapping for LUT-Based FPGAs
papers.task_relation: Defines the K-LUT mapping problem whose LUT count or level count the task scores; ABC's `if` command implements the method.
papers.primary_goal: Improve LUT-based FPGA technology mapping (area and delay) through better cut-based mapping and area recovery.

papers.title: Circuit Minimization with QBF-Based Exact Synthesis
papers.task_relation: The record holder's method family (exact resynthesis of subcircuits) applied to benchmark circuits; an ABC script cannot express it, so the task is the script-restricted version.
papers.primary_goal: Minimise Boolean circuits by exact resynthesis of small subcircuits encoded as QBF.
